newsitem.title: INDIA: Seven Hindus killed in Kashmir gun attack.
newsitem.headline: Seven Hindus killed in Kashmir gun attack.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen shot dead seven local Hindus in a major act of violence in the troubled Himalayan region of Kashmir, police said on Saturday.
A police spokesman said the shooting took place late on Friday at Sangrampur, a village in Budgam district 20 km (12.5 miles) southwest of Srinagar, summer capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state.
"They have been living here all these years. All were male," the spokesman told Reuters. "We are still investigating."
Police said the attackers targeted eight people from five families. Seven died while the eighth was seriously injured but was now out of danger, police said.
Violence against Hindus in the province, the only Moslem-majority state in mainly Hindu India, is usually blamed on Islamic separatists.
No separatist group claimed responsibility for the killings, described by police as the biggest such incident involving local Hindus.
The attack was the first major act of violence against Hindus since September last year, when India held the first provincial elections in Jammu and Kashmir since 1987.
It came a week before a rare resumption of stalled high-level diplomatic talks between India and Pakistan, scheduled to start on March 28 in New Delhi.

Pakistan has fought two wars with India over the region since the two nations became independent from British rule in 1947. It denies routine Indian charges that it arms and trains Kashmiri separatist guerrillas.
Members of the state's legislative assembly, sitting in the winter capital of Jammu, condemned Friday's incident.
"The forthcoming Indo-Pakistan dialogue is meaningless unless the killings in Kashmir valley are stopped by Pakistan," Jammu and Kashmir's chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, told the assembly.
Kashmir's leading separatist organisation, the All-Parties' Hurriyat (freedom) Conference, which brings together some 30 religious and political groups, condemned the incident.
"We strongly condemn these brutal killings, they (Kashmiri Hindus) are a part and parcel of us," a Hurriyat spokesman said in Srinagar.

"The killing is the handiwork of anti-movement activists who want to defame the ongoing freedom struggle of Kashmir," the Hurriyat spokesman said. "We express our sympathies with the bereaved families."

More than 300,000 minority Hindus, called Pandits in the Himalayan valley, fled Kashmir after the beginning of the rebellion in 1990 in the region, where violence linked to insurgency has claimed more than 20,000 lives in seven years.
But a small number of Hindus remained in troubled Kashmir. The families of the victims of Friday's incident did not leave the valley and stayed in the village, local officials said.
In the last such incident, unidentified militants killed ten Hindu villagers including five members of a family in the Doda region in the southern Jammu region of the state in June 1996.
In April 1996, suspected separatist guerrillas shot dead eight Nepali Hindu workers near Srinagar.
In July 1996, six Indian Hindu tourists were shot dead by unidentified militants near Srinagar's famous Dal Lake. In the same month, 11 migrant Hindu workers were killed in northern Kashmir.
